sections.title: The letter u
paragraphs: The letter name is (u) /u/. Its main sound appears in the word (um) /ˈũ/, which means one, a. This letter has three different sounds.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, pull your tongue back and lift it high. Push your lips forward into a small circle. Turn your voice on. Next, make this same motion very quickly as a glide. For the last sound, let the air flow through both your mouth and your nose at the same time. Put a hand on your throat to feel the voice shake.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: When stressed or before vowels, it makes its primary sound, as in (uva) /ˈu.vɐ/ or (luta) /ˈlu.tɐ/. In a diphthong, which means two vowel sounds in one syllable, it acts as a quick glide, heard in (mau) /ˈmaw/ and (quase) /ˈkwa.zɨ/. Before nasal consonants in the same syllable, it becomes a nasal vowel, as in (junto) /ˈʒũ.tu/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not add an extra sound before it like the sound in cute. Push your lips out tightly and start with the vowel immediately, as in blue. Do not drop the glide in a diphthong, but pronounce it smoothly. When air flows through the nose, keep your mouth open and do not add an English consonant sound like the one in ring.
